ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r16.speaker: Şerh-i Lübâb
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r16.claim: Adab includes greeting with assalamu alaykum, standing for supplication, sitting according to the deceased's former status if needed, and reciting whatever Quran is easy, including the listed surahs and repeated Ikhlas.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r16.anchor: Sonra kāimen dua eder, oturursa hâl-i hayâtındaki mertebesine göre uzak veya yakın oturur ve Kur’an’dan kolayına geleni okur.

ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r17.speaker: İbn Âbidîn
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r17.claim: Ibn Abidin details the dedication of recitation and other acts' rewards to the deceased; the jurists allow transferring rewards from prayer, fasting, charity, and other deeds.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r17.anchor: insan, salât veya savm veya sadaka veya diğer amelinin sevâbını başkasına yapabilir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r18.speaker: Tatarhâniyye
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r18.claim: The best practice is to intend one's charity for all believing men and women, since its reward reaches them without reducing one's own.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r18.anchor: Tasadduk eden için efdal olan cemî‘-i mü’minîn ve mü’minât için niyet etmektir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r19.speaker: Hafız İbn Teymiyye
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r19.claim: Ibn Taymiyya wished to forbid dedicating Quran recitation's reward to the Prophet, arguing that it requires his specific permission and that one should instead send blessings and ask for wasila.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r19.anchor: Hafız İbn Teymiyye, kıraat sevâbının Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’ne ihdâsını men‘etmek istemiş

ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r20.speaker: Sübkî ve daha diğerleri
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r20.claim: Subki and others reject Ibn Taymiyya's restriction, arguing that no specific permission is needed and citing Ibn Umar and others.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r20.anchor: Sübkî ve daha diğerleri ise bu

ELMALILI:102:1-5#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#4/r1.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:102:1-5#4/r1.claim: In advice to Abu Yusuf, Abu Hanifa counsels measured private correction of a ruler, debate with an heretical ruler through Quran and Sunnah, prayer for protection if rejected, remembrance of death, forgiveness for teachers, continued recitation, and frequent visits to graves, shaykhs, and blessed places.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#4/r1.anchor: Üstâdın ve kendilerinden ilim ahzettiğin kimseler için istiğfar eyle ve tilâvete devam et, kubûru ve meşâyıhı ve mevâzi‘-i mübarekeyi çok ziyaret eyle.

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.claim: Reports on grave visitation establish its legitimacy, wisdom, timing, method, and etiquette.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.anchor: ziyâret-i kubûrun da meşrûiyetini, hikmetini, zamanını, usul ve âdâbını göstermektedir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.claim: Visitation does not entail asking the dead for help or invoking them; visitors greet them and ask Allah for safety for living and dead alike.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.anchor: ölülerden bir şey istemek, “yetiş yâ fülân” gibi istimdad etmek yoktur

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.claim: Visitors may recite Qur'an and dedicate its reward, while seeking Allah's will and preparing in complete faith for their own death.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.anchor: Kur’an okuyup sevâbını hediye etmek ve bilhassa geridekilerin de onlara iltihak edeceğini düşünerek

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.claim: The visit should prompt reflection on resurrection, judgment, the scales, and the destinations of deeds, strengthening resolve for faith and righteous action over rivalry and accumulation.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.anchor: bütün kalbiyle âhireti, sonunda o kabirlere gidileceği ve o kabirlerin deşileceği

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.claim: The dead have returned or been returned to Allah and enter their final states according to their standing before Him.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.anchor: Ölenler, indallah mertebelerine göre ya îşe-i râzıyeye

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.claim: A prophetic report says a person will be resurrected with those he loves, so those who love the good join the good and those who love evil join the evil.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.anchor: اَلْمَرْءُ مَعَ مَنْ أَحَبَّ sevdikleriyle haşrolunacaklarından iyileri sevenler iyilerle

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.claim: Love is valuable when it is for Allah and follows the command to follow the Prophet.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.anchor: Sevginin kıymeti de وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَشَدُّ حُبًّۭا لِّلَّهِ

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.claim: The dead have passed on: their deeds are theirs and yours are yours, so boasting or competing over them has no point.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.anchor: Onların kazancı kendilerine, sizin kazancınız sizedir; siz onların amellerinden mes’ul olacak değilsinizdir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.claim: Worship and seeking aid belong to Allah; helping people for Allah is praised, while begging people is blameworthy, and asking the dead is especially unfitting.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.anchor: ibadet ve isti‘âne ise ancak Allah’adır. Allah için halka i‘âne memduh

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.claim: One benefits from the deceased by reflecting on their lives and works and keeping their good example alive.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.anchor: Onlardan istifade onların ahvâl ve sîretlerini düşünerek ilmî, amelî eserlerinden

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.speaker: İbn Âbidîn
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.claim: Saints differ in their nearness to Allah, and visitors benefit in proportion to their own knowledge and insight into them.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.anchor: Onun için İbn Âbidîn [6053] rahmetullâhi aleyh

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.claim: A grave visit can affect a person like reading a book, awakening memories and reflection.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.anchor: Bir kabri ziyaretle bir kitap okur gibi tefekkürün uyandıracağı hatıralara göre bir tesir alması

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.claim: The best visit awakens the afterlife through tenderness of heart and sends the visitor back to life resolved to spend the remaining years in good works.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.anchor: âhiret hissini duyup o intibah ile hayâta dönmek ve gaflet perdesini sıyırıp kalan ömrünü hayr u hasenât ile

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.claim: A hadith says grave visitation reminds people of the afterlife.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.anchor: hadîs-i şerifte buna “çünkü o size âhireti tezekkür ettirir” diye tenbih buyurulmuştur

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.claim: Visiting graves to boast and compete reverses their proper lesson and expresses extreme hardheartedness and heedlessness, prompting the rebuke of 102:1–2.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.anchor: tefâhur gurûruyla tekâsür için yapmak kasvetin, gafletin son derecesi olduğundan dolayı

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.claim: On a literal reading, competition may end when graves are visited, or grave visitation itself may end worldly greed.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.anchor: yani kabirleri ziyaret ettiğiniz zaman o tekâsür ve ilhâ kalmadı

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.claim: Exegetes generally take grave visitation here as a metaphor for death, since death certainly ends competition.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.anchor: müfessirîn bu takdirde kabir ziyareti hakikat mânasına olmayıp ölümden kinaye olacağını söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.claim: Seeing a dead person, attending burial, or later visiting a grave can awaken reflection in receptive hearts, but this is not universal and is derivative of death.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.anchor: kalbi olanlara bu intibah ve tezkir hükmü inkişaf etmez değil ise de, bu umûmî ve kat‘î olmadığı gibi

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.claim: If literal visitation were intended, the wording would encourage a required or recommended practice, conflicting with the following rebuke.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.anchor: memnû‘ve mezmum değil, kelâmın sevki gayeye müteveccih

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.claim: The passage's purpose is to rebuke heedlessness and rivalry, not to promote grave visitation; this resolves the tension with the following prohibition.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.anchor: kelâmın mâ-sîka-lehi ziyâret-i kubûr değil ilhâ ve tekâsür ile tevbihtir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.claim: The warning can mean that rivalry deludes people until their souls leave and their bodies enter the graves.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.anchor: Tekâsür sizleri öyle iğfal etti ki tâ canlarınız çıkıncaya, tenleriniz kabirlere girinceye kadar

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.claim: The rebuke warns people not to waste worldly life in rivalry; they will learn the gravity and outcome of their heedlessness later.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.anchor: sonu kabre varan dünyada ehem olan vazifeyi unutup da boş, fâni şeylerle eğlenip oyalanmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r5.claim: Maqabir is the plural of maqbara, meaning graves; commentators read “you visited the graves” metaphorically as dying while the contest continued, metaphorically as boasting over the dead, or literally as visiting graves to boast.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r5.anchor: Müfessirler özellikle şu mânaları vermişlerdir: a) Mecazi anlamda, “Sonunda ölüp kabirlere girdiniz; bu tutku ve yarış sizde ölünceye kadar sürüp gitti”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r6.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r6.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs boasted of abundant wealth, children, kin, and servants, then visited ancestors' graves to prove their tribe's superiority through its many notable dead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r6.anchor: Câhiliye Arapları mal, evlât, akraba ve hizmetçilerinin çokluğunu bir gurur ve şeref sebebi sayarlar, hatta bu hususta övünürken yaşayanlarla yetinmeyip kabilelerinin üstünlüğünü geçmişleriyle de ispat etmek için kabirlere gider

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.claim: Even if reports describe a specific occasion, the general target is human boasting in abundant wealth, offspring, and supporters; true superiority appears in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.anchor: genel anlamda insan fıtratındaki mal, evlât ve taraftarların çokluğu ile övünme vb. davranışlar eleştirilmekte, gerçek üstünlüğün âhirette ortaya çıkacağı belirtilmektedir

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.speaker: ابن بريدة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Ansar tribes Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith competed by boasting about their living members, then went to the graves and boasted of the dead; the surah was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في قبيلتين من الأنصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث تفاخروا وتكاثروا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.speaker: علي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Muslims doubted punishment in the grave until the passage from “competition distracts you” through “then you will know” was revealed regarding that punishment.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.anchor: كنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت ﴿ ألهاكم التكاثر ﴾ إلى ﴿ ثم كلا سوف تعلمون ﴾ في عذاب القبر

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say the passage concerns Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm competing over which clan had more notables, then counting their dead at the graves; Banū Sahm had more.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في حيين من قريش: بني عبد مناف وبني سهم كان بينهم لحاء فتعاند السادة والأشراف أيهم أكثر

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.claim: Qatāda offers another view: the verse concerns Jews boasting that one group outnumbered another until death carried them off in error.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود، قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان وبنو فلان أكثر من بني فلان، ألهاهم ذلك حتى ماتوا ضلالا.

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.claim: One interpretation says greed for wealth distracts people until death and only then do they bequeath funds for alms and pilgrimage.
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.anchor: الحرص على المال وطلب تكثيره حتى منعتم الحقوق المالية

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.claim: Another interpretation says accumulation distracts from religion; people have hearts like stones that soften only when they visit graves, though even this slight response is inadequate.
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.anchor: فلا تلتفتون إلى الدين ، بل قلوبكم كأنها أحجار لا تنكسر

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r3.claim: Leaving the object of distracted unspecified makes the rebuke broader, covering neglect of remembrance, obligations, recommended acts, knowledge, worship, reflection, and contemplation.

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.claim: Read in context, accumulation distracts either from preparing for the Calamity before death or from remembering the grave until people reach it.
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر عن التدبر في أمر القارعة والاستعداد لها قبل الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.speaker: أبو بريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.claim: Although many call the surah Meccan, al-Alusi chooses Medina based on Abu Burayda's report: two Ansari clans boast of living ancestors, then go to the graves to boast of the dead, prompting its revelation. A report from Ubayy says the warning about Adam's desire for a third valley continued until the surah descended; Ali says it ended doubts about grave punishment, which al-Alusi takes as Medinan evidence because that punishment is mentioned in a Medinan context.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.anchor: عن أبي بريدة فيها قال نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الانصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث تفاخروا وتكاثروا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.claim: Ibn al-Milq explains the thousand-verse merit as one sixth of the Qur'an's roughly 6,200 verses: al-Ghazali's six aims include knowledge of the return to God, which this surah contains. Al-Alusi says the matter lies beyond this calculation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.anchor: ذكر ناصر الدين بن الميلق في سر ذلك أن القرآن ستة آلاف ومائتا آية وكسر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p275/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p275/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p275/r1.claim: Although rhetoricians notice the cadence of al-maqābir, its broader sense is decisive: it evokes the gathering of the dead across ages and classes, unlike qubūr, and suits the end of worldly accumulation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p275/r1.anchor: واستعمالها هنا هو الملائم معنوياً لهذا التكاثر، دلالة على مصير ما يتكالب عليه المتكاثرون في حطام الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.claim: Calling their mention of the dead “visiting the graves” is a sarcastic way to describe the rivals' conduct.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.anchor: عبر عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى بزيارة المقابر تهكما بهم

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r1.claim: The phrase can mean you died and your bodies visited their graves: rivalry over wealth, children, and numbers occupied your lives until death.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r1.anchor: قيل : { حتى زرتم } : أي متم وزرتم بأجسادكم مقابرها ، أي قطعتم بالتكاثر والمفاخرة بالأموال والأولاد

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r2.speaker: أعرابي
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r2.claim: A Bedouin, hearing the verse, swore by the Kaaba that the people were sent toward resurrection, since a visitor departs rather than staying.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r2.anchor: وسمع بعض الأعراب { حتى زرتم } فقال : بعث القوم للقيامة ، ورب الكعبة فإن الزائر منصرف لا مقيم

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r3.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r3.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz is reported to have expressed a view similar to the Bedouin's, that grave visitors depart rather than remain.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r3.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز نحو من قول الأعرابي

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the wording evokes repeated grave visits to outdo predecessors and amplify their renown.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r4.anchor: وقيل : هذا تأنيث على الإكثار من زيارة تكثرا بمن سلف وإشادة بذكره

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r5.claim: The Prophet first forbade visiting graves, then permitted it for taking admonition, not for boasting or rivalry; no grading is given.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r5.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن زيارة القبور

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya condemns practices such as frequenting graves, marking them with stones or marble, decorating them as honor, and displaying mausoleums.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية : كما يصنع الناس في ملازمتها وتسليمها بالحجارة والرخام ، وتلوينها شرفا

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan says Ibn Atiyya knew only Andalusian graves and criticizes the greater ostentation and wasted wealth in Cairo's cemeteries.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r7.anchor: وابن عطية لم ير إلا قبور أهل الأندلس ، فكيف لو رأى ما تباهى به أهل مصر في مدافنهم

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan criticizes some self-described Sufis who spend their time visiting and boasting of saints' tombs and journeys, memorize their stories, yet lack knowledge of ablution's duties and sunnas while receiving public and royal support.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r8.anchor: وأما التباهي بالزيارة ، ففي هؤلاء المنتمين إلى الصوف أقوام ليس لهم شغل إلا زيارة القبور

ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r9.claim: He also criticizes wonder-working claims of secret “Khidr knowledge”; scholars imitate these stories mixed with a little learning to seek money, status, and hand-kissing, and he prays for God's guidance.
ABUHAYYAN:102:2/r9.anchor: وأما من شذا منهم لأن يتكلم للعامة فيأتي بعجائب ، يقولون هذا فتح هذا من العلم اللدني علم الخضر

ALUSI:102:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r1.claim: They counted all the living, then went to the graves and mentioned those buried there, competing in the number of the dead; the endpoint is included in the process.
ALUSI:102:2/r1.anchor: حتى إذا استوعبتم عدد الأحياء صرتم إلى المقابر وانتقلتم إلى ذكر من فيها فتكاثرتم بالأموات

ALUSI:102:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ALUSI:102:2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm competed in numbers; after the first counted the living, the second counted the dead and won.
ALUSI:102:2/r2.anchor: وعن الكلبي ومقاتل أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا أيهم أكثر عددا

ALUSI:102:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r3.claim: For the earlier occasion, grave-visiting is literal; in the clan story it means reaching the point of mentioning the dead, by metonymy or metaphor, and is best treated as a representation.
ALUSI:102:2/r3.anchor: وزيارة المقابر على ما تقدم على ظاهرها وأما على هذا فقد عبر بها عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى

ALUSI:102:2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r4.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI:102:2/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf reads the phrase as sarcastic: they act like people visiting graves without a sound purpose.

ALUSI:102:2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers that grave visits should prompt reflection on death, but the boasters perversely made them a cause of heedlessness.

ALUSI:102:2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r6.claim: Boasting distracts from religion, the most important concern; suppressing the object of distraction magnifies it and intensifies the blame, condemning anything that distracts.
ALUSI:102:2/r6.anchor: وحذف الملهى عنه للتعظيم المأخوذ من الإبهام بالحذف والمبالغة في الذم

ALUSI:102:2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI:102:2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan explain that wealth and children distract people until death, with grave-visiting standing for dying.
ALUSI:102:2/r7.anchor: وصدره قد أخرجه ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس وهو ابن أبي حاتم وابن أبي شيبة عن الحسن

ALUSI:102:2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r8.speaker: جرير
ALUSI:102:2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī cites an anonymous poem and Jarīr to show that visiting the graves can mean dying; the wording also points to resurrection.
ALUSI:102:2/r8.anchor:
وقال جرير :
زار القبور أبو مالك

ALUSI:102:2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r9.claim: An Arab heard the verse and concluded that the people would be raised for Judgment, since a visitor eventually leaves rather than remaining.
ALUSI:102:2/r9.anchor: يحكى أن أعرابيا سمع ذلك فقال بعث القوم للقيامة ورب الكعبة

ALUSI:102:2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r10.speaker: مر بن عبد العزيز
ALUSI:102:2/r10.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz says every visitor must return either to the Garden or the Fire; the verse also signals the short stay in graves.
ALUSI:102:2/r10.anchor: وعن مر بن عبد العزيز أنه قال لا بد لمن زاد أن يرجع

ALUSI:102:2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r11.claim: The past tense indicates certainty, may include those who died first, or treats the ancestors' deaths as the listeners' own.
ALUSI:102:2/r11.anchor: والتعبير بالماضي لتحقق الوقوع أو لتغليب من مات أولا أو لجعل موت آبائهم بمنزلة موتهم

ALUSI:102:2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI:102:2/r12.claim: Abū Muslim says God addresses the sūra to unbelievers on Judgment Day, reproaching them for graves they had already visited; al-Ālūsī finds this astonishing.
ALUSI:102:2/r12.anchor: قول أبي مسلم أن الله عز وجل يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة تعييرا للكفار

ALUSI:102:2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:102:2/r13.claim: Another view takes the verse as reproaching excessive grave visits made to boast of the dead and one's visits rather than remember the afterlife.
ALUSI:102:2/r13.anchor: وقيل هذا تأنيب على الإكثار من زيارة القبور تكثرا بمن سلف ومباهاة

ALUSI:102:2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī says that reading is far from the verse, though he cites the report that grave visits should remind one of the afterlife.
ALUSI:102:2/r14.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الآية بمعزل عن ذلك نعم لا كلام في ذم زيارة القبور

ALUSI:102:2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r15.claim: He condemns visiting graves to boast of the deceased or the visit, especially ignorant shrine-goers who treat innovations and abuses as acts of worship.
ALUSI:102:2/r15.anchor: نعم لا كلام في ذم زيارة القبور للتفاخر بالمزور أو للتباهي بالزيارة

BAGHAWI:102:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:102:2/r1.claim: Visiting the graves means that you died and were buried.

BAGHAWI:102:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI:102:2/r2.claim: Qatāda says the sūra was revealed about Jews who boasted that their clans outnumbered others, remaining distracted until they died astray.

BAGHAWI:102:2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r3.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI:102:2/r3.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm competed over nobles and numbers; after ʿAbd Manāf first counted more living people, Sahm counted the dead and won by three households.
BAGHAWI:102:2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي : نزلت في حيين من قريش

BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.claim: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports from his father that the Prophet explained a person's wealth is only what he consumes, wears out, or gives away and sends ahead.
BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.anchor: عن مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير ،   عن أبيه

BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that three follow the dead, but family and wealth return while deeds remain.
BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.anchor: أنس بن مالك يقول :  "  قال رسول الله

BAYDAWI:102:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:102:2/r1.claim: Once they had counted all the living, they turned to the graves and boasted of the dead; visiting graves figuratively describes recalling the dead.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r1.anchor: إذا استوعبتم عدد الأحياء صرتم إلى المقابر

BAYDAWI:102:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r2.speaker: رُوي
BAYDAWI:102:2/r2.claim: Banū ʿAbd Manāf first outnumbered Banū Sahm; Sahm then proposed counting both living and dead, and claimed superiority.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r2.anchor: روي أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا بالكثرة

BAYDAWI:102:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r3.speaker: بنو سهم
BAYDAWI:102:2/r3.claim: Banū Sahm said rivalry had destroyed them in the pre-Islamic age and challenged their rivals to count the living and dead.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r3.anchor: فقال بنو سهم : إن البغي أهلكنا في الجاهلية

BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.claim: The object of distraction—the religious matters that concern them—is omitted for grandeur and emphasis.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.anchor: وإنما حذف المنهي عنه وهو ما يعنيهم من أمر الدين للتعظيم والمبالغة

BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.claim: Another view takes the rivalry over wealth and children as lasting until death and burial, wasting life that should have prepared for the afterlife; visiting graves means dying.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم مضيعين أعماركم في طلب الدنيا

BIQAI:102:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:2/r1.claim: Calling burial a visit answers deniers who imagined permanent residence in graves and signals that resurrection must follow.

BIQAI:102:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:2/r2.claim: Even a long stay in the intermediate realm is brief beside lasting residence in Paradise or Hell; a visitor eventually returns to a settled home.
BIQAI:102:2/r2.anchor: وأن اللبث في البرزخ وإن طال فإنما هو كلبث الزائر عند مزوره في جنب الإقامة بعد البعث في دار النعيم أو غار الجحيم

BIQAI:102:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:2/r3.claim: They visit graves through dying and burial, when the time for deeds that save them has passed; death alone should deter them even before the greater events of judgment.
BIQAI:102:2/r3.anchor: لا تتمكنون من عمل ما ينجيكم

BIQAI:102:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r4.speaker: أعرابي
BIQAI:102:2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports that a Bedouin heard the verse and inferred resurrection, since a visitor departs rather than stays.

BIQAI:102:2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
BIQAI:102:2/r5.claim: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā reports that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said the graves are only a visit and one must return home, to Paradise or Hell.
BIQAI:102:2/r5.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه قرأها ثم قال

BIQAI:102:2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:102:2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the sūra to the preceding al-Qāriʿa: rivalry in numbers, kin, and family distracts from preparing for its terrors and is followed by threats.
BIQAI:102:2/r6.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

DURR:102:2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:2/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
DURR:102:2/r1.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz infers from calling the grave a visit that visitors must eventually leave it and return to their home.
DURR:102:2/r1.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه قرأ { الهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر } ثم قال : ما أرى المقابر إلا زيارة

IBNASHUR:102:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r1.claim: The phrase may mark the endpoint of ألهاكم: accumulation occupied them throughout life until they entered graves, where all action ceases.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { حتى زرتم المقابر } غاية ، فيحتمل أن يكون غاية لفعل { ألهاكم }

IBNASHUR:102:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r2.claim: On that reading the endpoint covers the whole duration of distraction, and visiting means coming to dwell in graves; calling it a visit hints that they will leave them again.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r2.anchor: فالغاية مستعملة في الإِحاطة بأزمان المغيَّا لا في تنهيته وحصول ضده لأنهم إذا صاروا إلى المقابر انقطعت أعمالهم كلها

IBNASHUR:102:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r3.claim: The past tense treats a future event as already past because its occurrence is certain.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r3.anchor: والتعبير بالفعل الماضي في { زرتم } لتنزيل المستقبل منزلة الماضي لأنه محقق وقوعه مثل : { أتى أمرُ اللَّه }

IBNASHUR:102:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r4.claim: Alternatively, حتى marks the end of what they compete to accumulate: they even count graves, as in the reported rivalry between Banu ʿAbd Manaf and Banu Sahm.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الغاية للمتكاثر بهِ الدالِّ عليه التكاثُر ، أي بكل شيء حتى بالقبور تعدونها

IBNASHUR:102:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r5.claim: On the rivalry interpretation, visiting is literal, and grave is used metonymically for its occupant, as illustrated by Arabic poetry.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r5.anchor: فتكون الزيارة مستعملة في معناها الحقيقي ، أي زرتم المقابر لتَعُدُّوا القبور ، والعرب يكنّون بالقبر عن صاحبه

IBNASHUR:102:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r6.claim: Al-Nabighah's verse naming graves at Damascus and Sidon illustrates the author's point that Arabs use grave metonymically for the person buried there.

IBNASHUR:102:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r7.speaker: عصام بن عبيد الزماني أو همام الرقاشي
IBNASHUR:102:2/r7.claim: A verse attributed uncertainly to ʿIsam ibn ʿUbayd al-Zamani or Hammam al-Raqashi uses grave to mean the person who will be buried.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r7.anchor: وقال عصام بن عُبيد الزّمَّاني ، أو همّام الرَّقَاشي : لو عُدَّ قَبْرٌ وقبرٌ كُنتُ أقربَهم

IBNASHUR:102:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r8.claim: مقابر is plural of maqbarah, with the middle consonant either fatḥah or ḍammah; it denotes land containing many graves.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r8.anchor: و{ المقابر } : جمع مقبَرة بفتح الموحدة وبضمها . والمقبرة الأرض التي فيها قبور كثيرة

IBNASHUR:102:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:2/r9.claim: The rebuke is followed by posthumous threat; كلا rebukes and cancels the idea that rivalry can continue to its supposed endpoint.
IBNASHUR:102:2/r9.anchor: والتوبيخ الذي استُعمل فيه الخبر أُتبع بالوعيد على ذلك بعد الموت ، وبحرف الزجر والإِبطال بقوله : { كلا سوف تعلمون }

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r1.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r1.claim: One group says people kept boasting of their fathers and predecessors, counting the dead and their decayed bones among their accomplishments.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r1.anchor: فقال قوم : حتى ذكرتم الموت في تفاخركم بالآباء والسلف ، وتكثرتم بالعظام الرمام

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that people died and physically visited their graves, allowing competition over numbers to consume their lifespans.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r2.anchor: وقال : المعنى : حتى متم وزرتم بأجسادكم مقابرها ، أي قطعتم بالتكاثر أعماركم

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r3.speaker: أعرابي
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r3.claim: A Bedouin who heard the verse exclaimed that the people had been raised for the Resurrection, since a visitor departs rather than staying.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا التأويل روي أن أعرابيا سمع هذه الآية فقال : بعث القوم للقيامة ورب الكعبة ، فإن الزائر منصرف لا مقيم

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r4.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r4.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz held this interpretation of visiting graves as death.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r4.anchor: وحكى النقاش هذه النزعة من عمر بن عبد العزيز

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r5.claim: Others take it as a rebuke for excessive grave visiting as a way to boast about ancestors and memorialize them, distracting visitors from worship and learning.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا تأنيب على الإكثار من زيارة القبور ، أي حتى جعلتم أشغالكم القاطعة بكم عن العبادة والتعلم زيارة القبور تكثرا

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r6.claim: Reports from ʿAlī and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say the Prophet first forbade grave visits, then permitted them with the caution not to speak obscenely; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the later permission is for reflection, not boasting.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : «كنت نهيتكم

IBNATIYYA:102:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya criticizes people who turn graves into displays by piling stones and marble, raising and ornamenting them, or building mausoleums.
IBNATIYYA:102:2/r7.anchor: وتسنيمها بالحجارة والرخام ، وتلوينها شرفا ، وبنيان النواويس عليها

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Surat al-Takathur as Meccan.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.anchor: مقدمة السورة: تفسير سورة التكاثر وهي مكية .

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r3.claim: The distraction continued until death brought them to the graves, making them inhabitants of them.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r3.anchor: وتمادى بكم ذلك حتى جاءكم الموت وزرتم المقابر ، وصرتم من أهلها ؟ !

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet explains that rivalry distracted people from obedience until death came; Ibn Kathir cites it through Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam from his father.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } عن الطاعة ، { حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } حتى يأتيكم الموت

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.claim: The Prophet says three follow the dead person—family, wealth, and deeds; the family and wealth return, while the deeds remain.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.anchor: سمع أنس بن مالك يقول : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " يتبع الميت ثلاثةٌ ، فيرجع اثنان ويبقى معه واحد

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.speaker: ابن بريدة
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.claim: Ibn Burayda says the verses were revealed about two Ansari tribes, Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith, who competed over living notable relatives and then boasted over the dead at their graves.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في قوله : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } قال : نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار ، في بني حارثة وبني الحارث

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.claim: Qatada says people boasted that they outnumbered other tribes, while their members continually died until all had become inhabitants of graves.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.anchor: وقال قتادة : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } كانوا يقولون : نحن أكثر من بني فلان

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r15.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r15.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the plain sense: people came to the graves and were buried in them.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r15.anchor: والصحيح أن المراد بقوله : { زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } أي : صرتم إليها ودفنتم فيها

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r16.speaker: رجل من الأعراب
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r16.claim: A Bedouin patient corrects the Prophet's wish that his fever be purifying, saying it is a fever that will send an old man to the graves; the Prophet affirms this.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r16.anchor: على رجل من الأعراب يعوده ، فقال :  " لا بأس ، طهور إن شاء الله " . فقال : قلت : طهور ؟ ! بل هي حمى تفور

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r17.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r17.claim: Ali reports that they remained uncertain about punishment in the grave until this sura was revealed.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r17.anchor: عن علي قال : ما زلنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ }

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r18.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r18.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the report from Ali about grave punishment gharīb.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r18.anchor: ورواه الترمذي عن أبي كُرَيب ، عن حَكَّام بن سلم{[30462]} [ به ]{[30463]} وقال : غريب

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r19.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r19.claim: Ibn Kathir relates Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's reflection that graves are a visit, and a visitor must eventually return to his home.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r19.anchor: فقال : يا ميمون ، ما أرى المقابر إلا زيارة ، وما للزائر بد من أن يرجع إلى منزله

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r20.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r20.speaker: أبو محمد
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r20.claim: Abu Muhammad explains that the visitor returns to a home in either Paradise or Hell.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r20.anchor: قال أبو محمد : يعني أن يرجع إلى منزله إلى جنة أو نار .

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r21.speaker: بعض الأعراب
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r21.claim: Ibn Kathir recounts that a Bedouin hearing the verse exclaimed that resurrection had happened that day, since a grave visitor will leave for another destination.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r21.anchor: وهكذا ذُكر أن بعضَ الأعراب سمع رجلا يتلو هذه الآية : { حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } فقال : بُعثَ اليوم

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r22.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r22.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r22.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the Bedouin's remark to mean that the visitor will leave the grave station for another abode.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r22.anchor: أي : إن الزائر سيرحل من مقامه ذلك إلى غيره .

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r2.claim: The distraction continued until death brought them to the graves, making them inhabitants of them.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r2.anchor: وتمادى بكم ذلك حتى جاءكم الموت وزرتم المقابر ، وصرتم من أهلها ؟ !

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet explains that rivalry distracted people from obedience until death came; Ibn Kathir cites it through Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam from his father.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } عن الطاعة ، { حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } حتى يأتيكم الموت

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r8.claim: The Prophet says three follow the dead person—family, wealth, and deeds; the family and wealth return, while the deeds remain.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r8.anchor: سمع أنس بن مالك يقول : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " يتبع الميت ثلاثةٌ ، فيرجع اثنان ويبقى معه واحد

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r12.speaker: ابن بريدة
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r12.claim: Ibn Burayda says the verses were revealed about two Ansari tribes, Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith, who competed over living notable relatives and then boasted over the dead at their graves.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r12.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في قوله : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } قال : نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار ، في بني حارثة وبني الحارث

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r13.claim: Qatada says people boasted that they outnumbered other tribes, while their members continually died until all had become inhabitants of graves.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } كانوا يقولون : نحن أكثر من بني فلان

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r14.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r14.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the plain sense: people came to the graves and were buried in them.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r14.anchor: والصحيح أن المراد بقوله : { زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } أي : صرتم إليها ودفنتم فيها

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r15.speaker: رجل من الأعراب
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r15.claim: A Bedouin patient corrects the Prophet's wish that his fever be purifying, saying it is a fever that will send an old man to the graves; the Prophet affirms this.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r15.anchor: على رجل من الأعراب يعوده ، فقال :  " لا بأس ، طهور إن شاء الله " . فقال : قلت : طهور ؟ ! بل هي حمى تفور

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r16.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r16.claim: Ali reports that they remained uncertain about punishment in the grave until this sura was revealed.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r16.anchor: عن علي قال : ما زلنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ }

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r17.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r17.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the report from Ali about grave punishment gharīb.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r17.anchor: ورواه الترمذي عن أبي كُرَيب ، عن حَكَّام بن سلم{[30462]} [ به ]{[30463]} وقال : غريب

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r18.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r18.claim: Ibn Kathir relates Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's reflection that graves are a visit, and a visitor must eventually return to his home.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r18.anchor: فقال : يا ميمون ، ما أرى المقابر إلا زيارة ، وما للزائر بد من أن يرجع إلى منزله

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r19.speaker: أبو محمد
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r19.claim: Abu Muhammad explains that the visitor returns to a home in either Paradise or Hell.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r19.anchor: قال أبو محمد : يعني أن يرجع إلى منزله إلى جنة أو نار .

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r20.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r20.speaker: بعض الأعراب
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r20.claim: Ibn Kathir recounts that a Bedouin hearing the verse exclaimed that resurrection had happened that day, since a grave visitor will leave for another destination.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r20.anchor: وهكذا ذُكر أن بعضَ الأعراب سمع رجلا يتلو هذه الآية : { حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } فقال : بُعثَ اليوم

IBNKATHIR:102:2/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r21.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r21.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the Bedouin's remark to mean that the visitor will leave the grave station for another abode.
IBNKATHIR:102:2/r21.anchor: أي : إن الزائر سيرحل من مقامه ذلك إلى غيره .

MAWARDI:102:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:102:2/r1.claim: One reading is that death brings people to the graves as visitors, from which they return to their home in Paradise or the Fire.
MAWARDI:102:2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : حتى أتاكم الموت فصرتم في المقابر زوّاراً ،   ترجعون منها كرجوع الزائر إلى منزله ،   من جنة أو نار .

MAWARDI:102:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:102:2/r2.speaker: الكلبي وقتادة
MAWARDI:102:2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi and Qatada report a rivalry between Quraysh's Banu ʿAbd Manaf and Banu Sahm: after counting the living, the clans counted their dead, and Sahm prevailed; the verses rebuked this numerically driven boasting and counting the dead.
MAWARDI:102:2/r2.anchor: ما حكاه الكلبي وقتادة : أن حيّين من قريش ،   بني عبد مناف وبني سهم ،   كان بينهما ملاحاة فتعادّوا بالسادة والأشراف أيهم أكثر

NASAFI:102:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:102:2/r1.claim: One reading is that death overtook them while they remained distracted in that state.
NASAFI:102:2/r1.anchor: حتى أدرككم الموت على تلك الحال

NASAFI:102:2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:102:2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:102:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they visited the graves and counted the dead among their own.
NASAFI:102:2/r2.anchor: أو حتى زرتم المقابر وعددتم من في المقابر من موتاكم

QURTUBI:102:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI:102:1/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi say two Quraysh clans, Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm, competed over notables and numbers; first the living, then the dead.
QURTUBI:102:1/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي : نزلت في حيين من قريش : بني عبد مناف ،   وبني سهم ،

QURTUBI:102:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:1/r13.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:102:1/r13.claim: Sa‘id reports from Qatada that the clans boasted about their numbers while their members died off until all became people of the graves.
QURTUBI:102:1/r13.anchor: وروى سعيد عن قتادة قال : كانوا يقولون نحن أكثر من بني فلان ،   ونحن أعد من بني فلان ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r1.claim: Death came and people became visitors to their graves; they will leave them again as a visitor returns home, to either Paradise or the Fire.
QURTUBI:102:2/r1.anchor: الثانية- قوله تعالى : { حتى زرتم المقابر } أي حتى أتاكم الموت ،   فصرتم في المقابر زوارا ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:102:2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that rivalry distracted people until they counted the dead as part of their competition.
QURTUBI:102:2/r2.anchor: وقيل : أي ألهاكم التكاثر حتى عددتم الأموات ،   على ما تقدم .

QURTUBI:102:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:102:2/r3.claim: Another view takes the verse as a threat: worldly boasting lasts until the people visit graves and see God’s punishment.
QURTUBI:102:2/r3.anchor: وقيل : هذا وعيد .   أي أشغلتم بمفاخرة الدنيا ،   حتى تزوروا القبور ،   فتروا ما ينزل بكم من عذاب الله عز وجل .

QURTUBI:102:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r4.claim: Maqābir is the plural of maqbara, pronounced with either a fatḥa or ḍamma on b; qubūr is the plural of qabr.
QURTUBI:102:2/r4.anchor: الثالثة-  " المقابر "  جمع مقبرة ومقبرة ( بفتح الباء وضمها ) .   والقبور : جمع القبر ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r5.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:102:2/r5.claim: The poem pictures the wealthy building stone structures over their graves and continuing to boast over the poor there.
QURTUBI:102:2/r5.anchor: أرى أهل القصور إذا أُمِيتُوا *** بَنَوْا فوقَ المقابِرِ بالصُّخُورِ

QURTUBI:102:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:102:2/r6.claim: A second poem uses maqbar for a burial place by people’s homes and says people decline while graves increase.
QURTUBI:102:2/r6.anchor: قال : لكل أناس مَقبَر بفِنائهم *** فهم ينقُصُونَ والقبورُ تَزِيدُ

QURTUBI:102:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r7.claim: Abu Sa‘id al-Maqburi was called al-Maqburi because he lived among the graves.
QURTUBI:102:2/r7.anchor: وهو المقبري والمقبري{[16334]} لأبي سعيد المقبري ،   وكان يسكن المقابر .

QURTUBI:102:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r8.claim: Qabartu means “I buried”; aqbartu means “I ordered that someone be buried.” Qurtubi points back to his discussion in Sura Abasa.
QURTUBI:102:2/r8.anchor: وقبرت الميت أقبره وأقبره قبرا ،   أي دفنته .   وأقبرته أي أمرت بأن يقبر .

QURTUBI:102:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r9.claim: This is the Qur’an’s only mention of graves; visiting them powerfully remedies hard hearts by recalling death and the Hereafter.
QURTUBI:102:2/r9.anchor: لم يأت في التنزيل ذكر المقابر إلا في هذه السورة .   وزيارتها من أعظم الدواء للقلب القاسي ؛

QURTUBI:102:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r10.claim: This reminder shortens hope, encourages detachment from worldly life, and reduces desire for it.
QURTUBI:102:2/r10.anchor: لأنها تذكر الموت والآخرة .   وذلك يحمل على قصر الأمل ،   والزهد في الدنيا ،   وترك الرغبة فيها .

QURTUBI:102:2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:102:2/r11.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud reports the Prophet’s instruction, after an earlier prohibition, to visit graves because they promote detachment from the world and remembrance of the Hereafter; Ibn Majah transmits it.
QURTUBI:102:2/r11.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور ،   فزوروا القبور ،   فإنها تزهد في الدنيا ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:102:2/r12.claim: In Sahih Muslim, Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying grave visits remind people of death.
QURTUBI:102:2/r12.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم من حديث أبي هريرة :  " فإنها تذكر الموت " .

QURTUBI:102:2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r13.speaker: بريدة
QURTUBI:102:2/r13.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits from Burayda that grave visits remind people of the Hereafter and grades the report hasan sahih.
QURTUBI:102:2/r13.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن بريدة :  " فإنها تذكر الآخرة "  .   قال : هذا حديث حسن صحيح ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:102:2/r14.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet cursed women who frequently visit graves, grades it hasan sahih, and mentions reports from Ibn Abbas and Hassan ibn Thabit in the chapter.
QURTUBI:102:2/r14.anchor: وفيه عن أبي هريرة : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  " لعن زوارات القبور "  .   قال : وفي الباب عن ابن عباس وحسان

QURTUBI:102:2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r15.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
QURTUBI:102:2/r15.claim: Some scholars say the prohibition preceded the Prophet’s later permission, which covered men and women.
QURTUBI:102:2/r15.anchor: وقد رأى بعض أهل العلم أن هذا كان قبل أن يرخص النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في زيارة القبور ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r16.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI:102:2/r16.claim: Other scholars disapprove of women visiting graves because of their lesser patience and greater grief.
QURTUBI:102:2/r16.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنما كره زيارة القبور للنساء لقلة صبرهن ،   وكثرة جزعهن .

QURTUBI:102:2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r17.claim: Qurtubi says scholars agree men may visit but differ about women; young women may not go out for this, while older women may.
QURTUBI:102:2/r17.anchor: قلت : زيارة القبور للرجال متفق عليه عند العلماء ،   مختلف فيه للنساء .   أما الشواب فحرام عليهن الخروج ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r18.claim: He allows women of every age to visit when separated from men, but forbids visits where or when mixing risks temptation and sin.
QURTUBI:102:2/r18.anchor: وجائز لجميعهن ،   ذلك إذا انفردن بالخروج عن الرجال ،   ولا يختلف في هذا إن شاء الله .

QURTUBI:102:2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r19.claim: To soften hard hearts, scholars advise remembering death, watching the dying, and visiting Muslim graves; direct sight has stronger effect than hearing a reminder, and grave visits are more accessible than witnessing a death.
QURTUBI:102:2/r19.anchor: قال العلماء : ينبغي لمن أراد علاج قلبه وانقياده بسلاسل القهر إلى طاعة ربه ،   أن يكثر من ذكر هاذم{[16336]} اللذات ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r20.claim: Visiting graves and witnessing the dying can remove hard-heartedness more effectively than remembering death alone because they provide direct sight.
QURTUBI:102:2/r20.anchor: فإن مشاهدة المحتضرين ،   وزيارة قبور أموات المسلمين ،   تبلغ في دفع ذلك ما لا يبلغه الأول ؛

QURTUBI:102:2/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:102:2/r21.claim: The Prophet’s saying “news is not like direct sight” explains why witnessing the dying and visiting graves can have stronger effect than remembering death.
QURTUBI:102:2/r21.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " ليس الخبر كالمعاينة "  رواه ابن عباس .

QURTUBI:102:2/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r22.claim: Watching someone die is not always possible, while graveyards are more readily found and their benefit more accessible.
QURTUBI:102:2/r22.anchor: وأما زيارة القبور فوجودها أسرع ،   والانتفاع بها أليق وأجدر .

QURTUBI:102:2/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r23.claim: A visitor should attend with a present heart and avoid sightseeing; the spectacle of graves is like that for an animal, and he should seek God and reform.
QURTUBI:102:2/r23.anchor: فإن هذه حاله تشاركه فيها بهيمة ،   ونعوذ بالله من ذلك .   بل يقصد بزيارته وجه الله تعالى ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r24.claim: The visitor should aim to please God, reform his heart, or benefit the deceased with Qur’an and prayer; he should not walk on or sit upon graves.
QURTUBI:102:2/r24.anchor: بل يقصد بزيارته وجه الله تعالى ،   وإصلاح فساد قلبه ،   أو نفع الميت بما يتلو عنده من القرآن والدعاء ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r25.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r25.claim: The visitor greets upon entering and at a known grave, approaching from the front as one would face a living person being addressed.
QURTUBI:102:2/r25.anchor: ويسلم إذا دخل المقابر ،   وإذا وصل إلى قبر ميته الذي يعرفه سلم عليه أيضا ،   وأتاه من تلقاء وجهه ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r26.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r26.claim: Reflect that the dead once commanded armies and amassed wealth, but death ended their hopes and left their families grieving and possessions divided.
QURTUBI:102:2/r26.anchor: ثم يعتبر بمن صار تحت التراب ،   وانقطع عن الأهل والأحباب ،   بعد أن قاد الجيوش والعساكر ،

QURTUBI:102:2/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:102:2/r27.speaker: author
QURTUBI:102:2/r27.claim: Recognize that one’s attachment to amusement and heedlessness about death resemble theirs, and that one will share their end; reflection redirects the heart to worship.
QURTUBI:102:2/r27.anchor: وليعلم أن ميله إلى اللهو واللعب كميلهم ،   وغفلته عما بين يديه من الموت الفظيع ،

RAZI:102:1/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r20.claim: Razi sees the grave-visiting wording as matching a past rivalry; the rebuke asks what it would profit people even if they were more numerous.
RAZI:102:1/r20.anchor: لأن قوله : { حتى زرتم المقابر } يدل على أنه أمر مضى

RAZI:102:1/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r21.claim: Visiting graves means going to a place, especially to soften the heart and remove love of worldly life; here grave-visitation perversely results from hard hearts and absorption in worldly love.

RAZI:102:1/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r22.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI:102:1/r22.claim: The Prophet says he had forbidden grave visits and then permits them, since visiting graves is a reminder.
RAZI:102:1/r22.anchor: على ما قال عليه السلام : «كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور ألا فزوروها

RAZI:102:1/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r24.claim: On the wealth interpretation, visiting graves is a euphemism for dying; the verse says that pursuit of wealth occupied people until death arrived.
RAZI:102:1/r24.anchor: أي حتى متم وزيارة القبر عبارة عن الموت

RAZI:102:1/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r25.speaker: جرير
RAZI:102:1/r25.claim: Jarīr's verse uses visiting graves to mean that Abū Mālik died, serving as poetic evidence for the euphemism.
RAZI:102:1/r25.anchor: قال جرير للأخطل : زار القبور أبو مالك *** فأصبح ألأم زوارها

RAZI:102:1/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r26.claim: An objection is that a visitor leaves after a while whereas the dead remain in their graves; Razi answers that a visitor must eventually depart and grave-dwellers likewise leave for the place of reckoning.
RAZI:102:1/r26.anchor: لكن لابد له من الرحيل ، وكذا أهل القبور يرحلون عنها إلى مكان الحساب

RAZI:102:1/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r27.claim: To explain the past tense for a future death, one possibility is that the address concerns people nearing death from old age, already standing at the brink of the grave.
RAZI:102:1/r27.anchor: كان مشرفا على الموت بسبب الكبر

RAZI:102:1/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r28.claim: Another answer reports the fate of earlier people as admonition to their successors, treating it as though it were news of the current audience because they follow the same way.
RAZI:102:1/r28.anchor: أن الخبر عمن تقدمهم وعظا لهم

RAZI:102:1/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r29.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI:102:1/r29.claim: Abū Muslim says God addresses unbelievers with this sura on Judgment Day, when their visits to graves have already occurred.
RAZI:102:1/r29.anchor: أبو مسلم : إن الله تعالى يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة

RAZI:102:1/r30.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r30.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r30.claim: A third view says greed for wealth prevented people from paying financial obligations until death, when they finally bequeathed money for zakat and pilgrimage.
RAZI:102:1/r30.anchor: الحرص على المال وطلب تكثيره حتى منعتم الحقوق المالية إلى حين الموت

RAZI:102:1/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r31.claim: A fourth view says rivalry turns hearts to stone, leaving only the small amount of religious feeling associated with visiting graves; Razi compares this with the rebuke that people give little thanks.
RAZI:102:1/r31.anchor: قلوبكم كأنها أحجار لا تنكسر البتة

RAZI:102:1/r35.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:1/r35.speaker: author
RAZI:102:1/r35.claim: Read with the following grave-visitation clause, the verse means that rivalry made people forget the grave until they actually visited it.

RAZI:102:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r1.claim: Ilhāʾ is turning someone toward diversion; lahw is turning aside toward what desire calls for, thereby neglecting something else.
RAZI:102:2/r1.anchor: الإلهاء الصرف إلى اللهو . واللهو الانصراف إلى ما يدعو إليه الهوى

RAZI:102:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r2.speaker: الزبير
RAZI:102:2/r2.claim: Razi cites a report that thunder made al-Zubayr leave his conversation, illustrating lahw as turning away.
RAZI:102:2/r2.anchor: ومنه الحديث : ( أن الزبير كان إذا سمع صوت الرعد لهى عن حديثه )

RAZI:102:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r3.claim: Takāthur means boasting against others in abundance of wealth, rank, and distinctions.
RAZI:102:2/r3.anchor: والتكاثر التباهي بكثرة المال والجاه والمناقب

RAZI:102:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI:102:2/r4.claim: Abu Muslim says tafāʿul may be reciprocal, affected or contrived, or intransitive; takāthur here permits the first two senses.
RAZI:102:2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : التكاثر تفاعل عن الكثرة والتفاعل يقع على أحد وجوه ثلاثة

RAZI:102:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r5.claim: In this verse takāthur can mean mutual rivalry, as each claims to exceed the other, or a person's effortful pursuit of ever greater wealth.
RAZI:102:2/r5.anchor: فيحتمل التكاثر بمعنى المفاعلة لأنه كم من اثنين يقول كل واحد منهما لصاحبه

RAZI:102:2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r6.claim: Razi treats takāthur and tafākhur as synonymous and links the wording to the description of worldly rivalry in 57:20.
RAZI:102:2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن التفاخر والتكاثر شيء واحد ونظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى : { وتفاخر بينكم }

RAZI:102:2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r7.claim: Human goods fall into spiritual goods of knowledge and virtue, bodily goods of health and beauty, and external goods such as wealth, status, kin, and friends.
RAZI:102:2/r7.anchor: وأجناس السعادة ثلاثة : ( فأحدها ) : في النفس ( والثانية ) : في البدن ( والثالثة ) : فيما يطيف بالبدن من خارج

RAZI:102:2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r8.claim: Razi cites Abraham's prayer for judgment and joining the righteous as exemplifying intellectual and moral goods, which yield lasting felicity.
RAZI:102:2/r8.anchor: وهما المرادان بقوله حكاية عن إبراهيم : { رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين }

RAZI:102:2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r9.claim: External goods serve the body: when a bodily part hurts, a person will sacrifice wealth and rank to save it.
RAZI:102:2/r9.anchor: إنما يراد كله للبدن بدليل أنه إذا تألم عضو من أعضائه فإنه يجعل المال والجاه فداء له

RAZI:102:2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r10.claim: The virtuous seek bodily health as a means to gain enduring spiritual goods through knowledge and action.
RAZI:102:2/r10.anchor: فالفضلاء من الناس إنما يريدونها للسعادة النفسانية فإنه ما لم يكن صحيح البدن لم يتفرغ

RAZI:102:2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r11.claim: Pursuing wealth, rank, helpers, and relatives privileges the lowest goods over knowledge and action, so it reverses the proper order and is blameworthy.
RAZI:102:2/r11.anchor: فالتفاخر بالمال والجاه والأعوان والأقرباء تفاخر بأخس المراتب من أسباب السعادات

RAZI:102:2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r12.claim: The condemned rivalry includes competition in numbers, wealth, status, relatives, allies, armies, and worldly pleasures generally.
RAZI:102:2/r12.anchor: ويدخل فيه التكاثر بالعدد وبالمال والجاه والأقرباء والأنصار والجيش

RAZI:102:2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r13.claim: Alhākum can be read as a statement about the audience or as an interrogative rebuke.
RAZI:102:2/r13.anchor: قوله : { ألهاكم } يحتمل أن يكون إخبارا عنهم ، ويحتمل أن يكون استفهاما بمعنى التوبيخ والتقريع

RAZI:102:2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r14.claim: The interrogative construal is supported by familiar alternative interrogative readings such as aʾ-andhartahum and aʾ-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman.
RAZI:102:2/r14.anchor: كما قرئ { أنذرتهم } و{ أأنذرتهم } ، و{ إذا كنا عظاما } و{ أئذا كنا عظاما }

RAZI:102:2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r15.claim: Razi relates that al-Abbas and Shayba boasted of the water-supply and key of the Kaaba, while Ali cited his fighting of unbelief; 9:19 was then revealed.
RAZI:102:2/r15.anchor: تفاخر العباس بأن السقاية بيده ، وتفاخر شيبة بأن المفتاح بيده

RAZI:102:2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r16.claim: Competition in genuine goods is not blameworthy: boasting of obedience and good character may be permitted when it is likely to inspire others to imitate.
RAZI:102:2/r16.anchor: يجوز للإنسان أن يفتخر بطاعاته ومحاسن أخلاقه إذا كان يظن أن غيره يقتدي به

RAZI:102:2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r17.claim: Takāthur is not universally condemned; the definite article identifies the familiar worldly rivalry that diverts people from worship, while competition in knowledge and virtue is praiseworthy.
RAZI:102:2/r17.anchor: فالألف واللام في التكاثر ليسا للاستغراق ، بل للمعهود السابق ، وهو التكاثر في الدنيا ولذاتها وعلائقها

RAZI:102:2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r18.claim: One reported occasion is the rivalry of Banū Sahm and Banū ʿAbd Manāf, who counted their living and dead members to determine which group was larger.
RAZI:102:2/r18.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في بني سهم وبني عبد مناف تفاخروا أيهم أكثر

RAZI:102:2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r19.claim: On the numbers reading, the verse rebukes them: even if they outnumbered their rivals, that would be of no benefit.
RAZI:102:2/r19.anchor: فكأنه تعالى يعجبهم من أنفسهم ، ويقول هب أنكم أكثر منهم عددا فماذا ينفع

RAZI:102:2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r20.claim: Visiting graves should soften the heart and loosen attachment to worldly life, but their immersion in it reverses the visit's proper effect.
RAZI:102:2/r20.anchor: وأهمها وأولاها بالرعاية ترقيق القلب وإزالة حب الدنيا فإن مشاهدة القبور تورث ذلك

RAZI:102:2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r21.speaker: النبي ﷺ
RAZI:102:2/r21.claim: Razi cites the Prophet's instruction to visit graves because doing so reminds people of death.
RAZI:102:2/r21.anchor: كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور ألا فزوروها فإن في زيارتها تذكرة

RAZI:102:2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r22.speaker: النبي ﷺ
RAZI:102:2/r22.claim: Through Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr from his father, Razi cites the Prophet's saying that a person owns only what was consumed, worn out, or given away.
RAZI:102:2/r22.anchor: ما روى مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير عن أبيه ، أنه عليه السلام كان يقرأ

RAZI:102:2/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r23.claim: A second view takes visiting the graves as a euphemism for dying: worldly acquisitiveness distracts people until death overtakes them.
RAZI:102:2/r23.anchor: والمراد من قوله : { حتى زرتم المقابر } أي حتى متم وزيارة القبر عبارة عن الموت

RAZI:102:2/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r24.speaker: جرير
RAZI:102:2/r24.claim: Jarīr's verse uses visiting graves to mean dying, describing Abū Mālik as having died.
RAZI:102:2/r24.anchor: قال جرير للأخطل : زار القبور أبو مالك *** فأصبح ألأم زوارها

RAZI:102:2/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r25.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r25.claim: Against the death reading, one may object that a visitor leaves while the dead remain; Razi replies that the dead too eventually leave for the place of reckoning.
RAZI:102:2/r25.anchor: أن الزائر هو الذي يزور ساعة ثم ينصرف ، والميت يبقى في قبره ، فكيف يقال

RAZI:102:2/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r26.claim: A second objection is that the verse uses past tense for death; one reply applies it to people already near death, said to stand at the grave's brink.
RAZI:102:2/r26.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد من كان مشرفا على الموت بسبب الكبر ، ولذلك يقال فيه

RAZI:102:2/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r27.claim: Another reply addresses the living through the example of their predecessors, as in the Qur'anic statement that earlier people killed prophets.
RAZI:102:2/r27.anchor: أن الخبر عمن تقدمهم وعظا لهم ، فهو كالخبر عنهم ، لأنهم كانوا على طريقتهم ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { ويقتلون النبيين }

RAZI:102:2/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r28.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI:102:2/r28.claim: Abū Muslim says the sūra addresses unbelievers on Judgment Day, when their visits to graves have already occurred.
RAZI:102:2/r28.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : إن الله تعالى يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة تعييرا للكفار

RAZI:102:2/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r29.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r29.claim: A third view says the pursuit of wealth kept people from paying financial duties until death, when they belatedly bequeathed money for zakat and pilgrimage.
RAZI:102:2/r29.anchor: الحرص على المال وطلب تكثيره حتى منعتم الحقوق المالية إلى حين الموت

RAZI:102:2/r30.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r30.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r30.claim: A fourth view says worldly rivalry hardens hearts until people reach the graves; their slight religious awakening is inadequate, like the rebuke “little do you give thanks.”
RAZI:102:2/r30.anchor: بل قلوبكم كأنها أحجار لا تنكسر البتة إلا إذا زرتم المقابر

RAZI:102:2/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r31.claim: The verse omits what rivalry distracts people from, making the rebuke broader: it encompasses remembrance, duties, recommended worship, knowledge, reflection, and contemplation.
RAZI:102:2/r31.anchor: وإنما لم يذكره ، لأن المطلق أبلغ في الذم لأنه يذهب الوهم فيه كل مذهب

RAZI:102:2/r32.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r32.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r32.claim: Read against the preceding sūra, rivalry distracts people from reflecting on the Calamity and preparing for it before death.
RAZI:102:2/r32.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر عن التدبر في أمر القارعة والاستعداد لها قبل الموت

RAZI:102:2/r33.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:102:2/r33.speaker: author
RAZI:102:2/r33.claim: Read forward, rivalry makes people forget the grave until they finally visit it.
RAZI:102:2/r33.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر ، فنسيتم القبر حتى زرتموه

TAB:102:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:102:2/r1.claim: The distracted people continue until they reach the graves and are buried there.
TAB:102:2/r1.anchor: يعني : حتى صرتم إلى المقابر فدفنتم فيها

TAB:102:2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:2/r2.speaker: author
TAB:102:2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī sees the warning that they will learn what they face upon reaching the graves as evidence that punishment in the grave is real.
TAB:102:2/r2.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على صحة القول بعذاب القبر ؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكره ، أخبر عن هؤلاء القوم الذين ألهاهم التكاثر

TAB:102:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:2/r3.speaker: علي
TAB:102:2/r3.claim: ʿAlī reports that they remained doubtful about punishment in the grave until Sūrat al-Takāthur was revealed, including its warning that they would soon know; al-Ṭabarī cites this report in several versions.
TAB:102:2/r3.anchor: عن زِرّ ، عن عليّ ، قال : كنا نشكّ في عذاب القبر ، حتى نزلت هذه الاَية : { ألهَاكَمُ التّكاثُرُ }
